output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by a vendor rule, not by release 6.14. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC, Corvane's rule-pack update added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17) that blocks password requests from Android's networking library. Blocks began at 10:41, and the added failures are all HTTP 403 rejections. They hit every app version, every Android OS version and phones with or without the security patch alike. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are untouched. About 92% of the blocked installs had logged in successfully before, so these are real customers, not bots. Rolling back 6.14 would not help, since 6.14 is only 5–10% of traffic and its success rate matches the others. Screen redesign, OS patch and auth-token change are not supported. The call-volume rise is likely partly fee notices, so that link is unproven. Next: ask Corvane to set the new rule to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping other protections, and confirm in telemetry that password success recovers. Don't raise bot sensitivity or exclude blocked attempts from the KPI; that would worsen lockouts and hide the problem. Continue the rollout while tracking by version. Confidence is high.
